timeline.event: Ono no Imoko is sent as Japan's envoy to the Sui court in China
Heijō-kyō (Nara) becomes Japan's capital
The Great Buddha of Tōdai-ji is dedicated in Nara
The capital moves to Heian-kyō, today's Kyoto
Murasaki Shikibu's Tale of Genji is read at the imperial court
timeline.label: c. 1008

timeline.event: Minamoto no Yoritomo is appointed shogun
A typhoon wrecks the second Mongol invasion fleet
Ashikaga Yoshimitsu begins his Golden Pavilion estate in Kyoto
Portuguese traders bring the first firearms to Tanegashima
Tokugawa Ieyasu wins the Battle of Sekigahara
Mount Fuji erupts for the last time so far
Commodore Perry's Black Ships arrive in Japan
The Meiji Restoration returns power to the emperor
Japan's first railway opens between Tokyo and Yokohama
The Great Kantō earthquake devastates Tokyo and Yokohama
Atomic bombs are dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki
The first Shinkansen bullet train line opens
Nintendo launches the Famicom games console
The Great Hanshin earthquake strikes Kobe
The Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami strike north-eastern Japan

places.name: Tokyo
places.clue: Until 1868 this megacity was called Edo, the seat of the Tokugawa shoguns.

places.name: Mount Fuji
places.clue: Japan's highest peak at 3,776 m, this near-perfect volcanic cone last erupted in 1707.

places.name: Kyoto
places.clue: Japan's imperial capital for over a thousand years, its temples include the gleaming Golden Pavilion and hillside Kiyomizu-dera.

places.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial
places.clue: The skeletal Atomic Bomb Dome was left standing in memory of the first city destroyed by a nuclear weapon.

places.name: Sapporo
places.clue: Host of Asia's first Winter Olympics in 1972, it fills its central park with giant snow sculptures each February.

places.name: Himeji Castle
places.clue: Nicknamed the White Heron for its gleaming white walls, it is the largest of Japan's surviving original castles.

places.name: Shirakawa-go
places.clue: Its steep thatched farmhouses, built to shed heavy snow, are said to resemble hands joined in prayer.

places.name: Shuri Castle, Okinawa
places.clue: This hilltop palace was the royal seat of the Ryukyu Kingdom, which ruled Okinawa for over 400 years.

places.name: Dōgo Onsen, Matsuyama
places.clue: One of Japan's oldest hot springs, its wooden bathhouse is said to have inspired the spirit bathhouse in Spirited Away.

places.name: Shiretoko Peninsula
places.clue: Brown bears roam this wild Hokkaido peninsula, whose coast sees the southernmost seasonal sea ice in the Northern Hemisphere.

places.name: Yakushima
places.clue: Its mossy cedar forests inspired Princess Mononoke, and one giant tree, Jōmon Sugi, is thought to be over 2,000 years old.

places.name: Chūson-ji, Hiraizumi
places.clue: Its Konjikidō hall, covered almost entirely in gold leaf, holds the mummified remains of the northern Fujiwara lords.
